title: Movies that you watch when you wanna feel something

commenti.body: [removed]
Fallen Angels (1995) since I often spend time alone, this film in some way “aestheticizes” loneliness and I have a desire to go for a walk alone around the city at night and think about the movie.

Synecdoche, New York

Mulholland Drive

The Shining

The Muppet Christmas Carol (once a year for obvious reasons)

In The Mood For Love

Paris, Texas

My parents got divorced when I was young, and I can see Aftersun being a staple on this list for me in future. I've only seen it once so far but found it really moving

I’ll say something unusual, but it’s guaranteed to make you feel many things: Cannbal Holocaust (1980). It’s an Italian found footage horror film, I believe the first of its kind. It absolutely lives up to its reputation as a foul, vile film that goes beyond anything that could be done today. I saw it a couple of days ago and can’t stop tho about it, it’s endlessly fascinating. I’ve never seen anything quite as effective at portraying human cruelty and evil. Of course, there’s violence of every kind being depicted on very realistic ways, so If you’re sensitive to that sort of thing, its better to stay away.
I gotta check this out def
[removed]

Before Sunrise always makes my heart ache in the best way possible. Other than that, my other "want to feel something" movies are About Time, EEAAO, La La Land, Interstellar, The Apartment, Synecdoche New York and Big Fish. I mean these are the ones that make me feel warm, there are other movies that make me feel strong emotions, but it's not emotions I seek out to feel better. Like Hereditary, which is one of my favorite movies of all time, but the strong emotions it makes me feel is depression, hopelessness, terror, anxiety and dread, so yeah, it's not something I want to relive often.
You sir have good taste (the muppets movie is one of the two best chistmas movies ever made, everything else is also good)

It's not my favorite movie, but goddamn does *Sense and Sensibility* (1995) earn its ending. Makes me (a 55-year-old guy) tear up every time.

Others for me include: *Corrina, Corrina* (1994) and *Dominick & Eugene* (1988). Both of those are small, character-driven dramas that, for me, are very emotional.

Although Malick’s filmography is pretty divisive, if you happen to have the luck to connect with it man oh man does it do something to your soul. To me, his films are transcendent; some of his films like To the Wonder and Tree of Life have one of the most arresting sequences I’ve ever had the privilege of seeing. His philosophy toward nature and love make him, in my opinion, one of the most spiritual and romantic of filmmakers. 

I also like La Haine.

I love the Before Sunrise trilogy so much. My kind of romance movies.
A lot of people shat on Knight of Cups but I really loved it.
I want to watch Aftersun but it sounds devastating. I don’t know if my heart can handle it.
I find it quietly devastating, on a very personal level. I don't think the film itself is *that* rough - it's probably more how you relate to the story.

The Deer Hunter. It's a wonderful life. The Searchers. Wolf of wall street. Django unchained. Boogie nights. The apartment. Doctor Zhivago. Fannie and Alexander. Scarface.
I like stuff.
It’s one of my favorite films and my personal favorite Malick.
